changes.historical_text: When an Equip Spell Card is equipped to this card, destroy the Equip Spell Card.
changes.summary: Era effect category, not a text erratum: the GOAT script declares the equip-destruction as EFFECT_TYPE_SINGLE+EFFECT_TYPE_CONTINUOUS - upstream's annotation 'effect is continuous' - and passes the destroy group through e:SetLabelObject/e:GetLabelObject, where the modern script declares EFFECT_TYPE_SINGLE+EFFECT_TYPE_TRIGGER_F and routes it through Duel.SetTargetCard/Duel.GetTargetCards with SetOperationInfo. In the era version the destruction is a Continuous Effect that starts no Chain, so the opponent cannot respond to it and it cannot miss timing; in the modern version it is a mandatory Trigger Effect that does both. Chronology unresolved.

review.notes: Text-versus-script conflict worth recording: the variant carries the v1 text (DB1-EN204, 2004-10-12), which narrows the wording to 'Equip Spell Card', but its destroy filter is identical to the modern one - s.filter(c,ec) returns c:GetEquipTarget()==ec - so it destroys ANY Equip Card equipped to Gearfried, a Union monster equipped as an Equip Card or an equipping Trap included. Upstream did not treat 'Equip Spell Card' as a narrowing, so the v1 -> v2 (SD5-EN005, 2005-11-02) restoration of 'Equip Card' has no implementation counterpart; it is recorded as cosmetic on the script evidence, with the tension flagged rather than resolved. The rest of the lineage is cosmetic: v2 -> v3 (LCJW-EN030, 2013-10-11) adds '(s)' and PSCT punctuation, v3 -> v4 (DPBC-EN022, 2015-06-19) swaps 'the' for 'that', v4 -> v5 (SS02-ENB10, 2019-01-24) adds 'If either player equips', which both scripts already do since the effect fires on EVENT_EQUIP irrespective of who equipped. These are collapsed here rather than into a change entry because they are trailing. Earlier v0 (PSV-101, 2002-10-20), 'Any Equip Card this card is equipped with is automatically destroyed', predates the baseline - and reads closer to what both scripts actually do than v1 does, which is part of why the v1 wording looks like a translation artefact rather than a behavioural narrowing.
